text.content:
Sect: Sabbat (revenant family)

Patron Clan: Tzimisce

The most rural and bestial of the revenant families, the Bratovitches hole up on remote, well-secured estates in North America, Poland, and a growing handful of South American holdings, breeding hellhounds and other unnatural animals to hunt Lupines and other enemies of the Sabbat. Outside of those hunts, they leave their land mainly to guide nomadic Sabbat packs or to abduct outsiders as breeding stock. Despite a reputation as inbred, homicidal hicks, established Bratovitch enclaves maintain real libraries, and the family supplies some of the Tzimisce's most valued research assistants on breeding projects.

Role: Hunters, animal-breeders, and wilderness guides for the Sabbat; specialists in tracking and destroying Lupines.

Disciplines: Animalism, Potence, Vicissitude

Weakness: Bratovitches are psychotic and unstable, suffering a two-Trait penalty on all tests to resist frenzy and a one-Trait penalty on social interactions with ordinary mortals.

Path: No Bratovitch follows Humanity — it simply doesn't take among them. Every other Path of Enlightenment appears with roughly equal frequency, including some all-but-abandoned Paths preserved by the family's more scholarly members.

Hellhounds: Bratovitches breed and surgically refine war-hounds for the Tzimisce and the wider Sabbat. Creating a hellhound from an ordinary dog requires mastery of both basic Animalism and basic Vicissitude, so only Bratovitches over 200 years old can make new ones; breeding existing hellhounds requires no Discipline at all, just nerve and veterinary skill. A hellhound fights with an aggravated bite and aggravated claws, hits like a Discipline-augmented predator (Celerity-, Fortitude-, and Potence-equivalent traits), and is roughly as tough as a vampire.
